identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Required, federated to the GitHub identity/account. Triggering a task requires a Copilot subscription (Pro, Pro+, Business, or Enterprise) and, for Business/Enterprise, an admin must enable the coding agent via the Policies page. The agent itself acts under a dedicated GitHub App/bot identity ('Copilot') with scoped repository/organization permissions rather than the user's full credentials; the human who delegated the task is recorded as co-author on commits. Authentication to GitHub is via the normal GitHub auth surfaces (web OAuth, GitHub CLI tokens). The agent is restricted from external data by authentication barriers plus a default firewall, and access to secrets is governed by repo/org settings.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Org/team-first, built on GitHub's existing permission and org model. Copilot Business/Enterprise admins control rollout via Policies; repository branch protections, rulesets, CODEOWNERS, and required-review rules all continue to apply to the agent's PRs. A key collaboration safeguard: the person who triggered the agent cannot approve the resulting PR (independent review enforced). Custom instructions can be shared org-wide (organization-level instructions auto-applied across repos). Multiple team members can delegate tasks to the agent in the same repo; collaboration happens through standard GitHub PR review/comment flows.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A workspace is effectively a single GitHub repository. The agent is strictly repo-scoped: one repository, one PR per task; it cannot span multiple repos or open multiple PRs from a single issue. There is no separate abstract 'workspace' entity — the repo (plus its branches, issues, and Actions environment) is the unit of scope. Work is materialized as an ephemeral checkout of the repo inside a GitHub Actions-hosted environment, and output lands on a `copilot/`-prefixed branch within that same repo.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Sessions are bound to a repository and to a specific task (an issue or a prompt). Each task spins up its own agent session in a fresh ephemeral environment and produces one PR. Sessions are tied to the GitHub identity of the delegator and are tracked per-repo. A user/repo can have multiple concurrent agent sessions (different tasks/issues at once), but each session is isolated to its own ephemeral environment and its own PR; sessions do not share a live workspace. The separate Copilot CLI maintains its own local/remote sessions with cross-device sync, distinct from the cloud coding-agent sessions.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Repo-level context = the cloned repository contents plus instruction files (AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, path-specific .github/instructions/*.instructions.md) and the copilot-setup-steps.yml environment config. Org-level context = organization-wide custom instructions auto-applied across repos. Session-level context = the issue/PR text, the conversation/feedback in PR comments, and the session's tool-execution log. Tool context can be extended per-repo/org via MCP servers (allow-listed). The agent's environment is otherwise sealed: it only sees what is checked into the repo or produced as Actions artifacts.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Multiple instruction sources are all supplied to the model, with conflict-resolution priority: (1) personal/user-level instructions highest, then (2) repository instructions. Supported files: .github/copilot-instructions.md (repo-wide, recommended < ~1000 words); path-specific .github/instructions/*.instructions.md (applied when the worked-on file matches the glob; cloud-agent and code-review only on GitHub.com); AGENTS.md (agent workflow instructions, root or nested anywhere — the NEAREST AGENTS.md in the directory tree takes precedence among agent-instruction files); plus CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are also read for cross-tool compatibility. Custom agents are defined in .github/agents/*.agent.md (YAML frontmatter: name, description, tools, mcp-servers) and support handoffs (Plan -> Implement -> Review). When both repo-wide and path-specific match, both sets are used together.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not applicable. Grounding is the repository codebase (cloned into the ephemeral environment), not a curated document/source set. There is no NotebookLM/Perplexity-Space-style bounded corpus. External knowledge can only be added via allow-listed MCP servers or by what is committed to the repo; the default firewall blocks arbitrary external retrieval.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Two distinct surfaces. (1) Cloud coding agent: the execution environment is ephemeral (GitHub Actions-backed container destroyed after each session); durable outputs are persisted as Git artifacts — the copilot/ branch, the PR, signed/verified commits, and the session logs stored on GitHub and linked from each commit via an Agent-Logs-Url trailer. So persistence is via GitHub's own storage (Git objects, PR/issue data, session-log storage), not a user-managed DB; no filesystem state survives between runs. (2) Copilot CLI (separate): session state is stored in the user's home directory, with user settings isolated from internal state, supporting cross-device sync and location-based permission persistence.
persistence_and_history.session_history: Coding-agent session logs are first-class and durable on GitHub: viewable via the agents panel/page, VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse, the GitHub CLI, Raycast, and the PR timeline ('View session', streamed live while running). Logs capture setup-step output, repo clone, firewall startup, and the agent's actions. Every agent commit links back to its full session logs (Agent-Logs-Url trailer) for permanent traceability/audit. The Copilot CLI separately persists conversation context, tool-execution logs, and permission decisions, resumable via `copilot --continue`, `copilot --resume`, or `copilot --resume SESSION-ID`. [uncertain] Exact on-disk/storage format and retention window for cloud session logs are not publicly documented.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Durable cross-session 'memory' is user-authored, not auto-generated: it lives in repo instruction files (AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, path-specific instructions) and org-level instructions, which the agent reads on every task. Ephemeral per-session state lives only in the ephemeral environment and the session log/PR conversation and is discarded when the environment is destroyed. The `/chronicle` slash command (Copilot CLI) analyzes recent sessions to suggest/auto-update .github/copilot-instructions.md — a semi-automated bridge from session experience into durable instructions. There is no described automatic semantic long-term memory store for the cloud agent.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Sessions are browsable and traceable per-repo via the agents panel/page, IDE integrations, and the commit -> session-log links; commits are searchable through normal Git/GitHub history. The Copilot CLI offers a session picker (`--resume`) to retrieve prior sessions by ID. [uncertain] Whether there is full-text or semantic search ACROSS many past cloud agent sessions (versus per-PR/per-commit navigation and a CLI picker) is not clearly documented; retrieval appears primarily navigational/ID-based rather than a global search index.
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: The execution environment is strictly ephemeral: an isolated GitHub Actions compute environment is created per session and destroyed at session end, with no filesystem/env state persisting between runs. Durable artifacts (branch, PR, commits, session logs) persist in GitHub under normal repo/Git retention. [uncertain] Explicit TTL/expiration or deletion policy for stored session logs, and whether logs are archived vs hard-deleted, are not publicly specified; they follow GitHub's platform/enterprise retention settings.

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: Each task runs in a secure, ephemeral, isolated development environment powered by GitHub Actions (Linux/Ubuntu x64 runners only), created fresh per session and destroyed afterward. Network egress is controlled by a firewall enabled BY DEFAULT that blocks outbound connections to unauthorized hosts to prevent code/data exfiltration; external services require explicit allow-listing (and MCP servers can be granted). The agent can only push to non-protected branches (typically copilot/-prefixed), never directly to main/master; branch protections and rulesets still apply. The agent runs under a scoped GitHub App identity, not the user's full credentials. Output PRs are scanned by CodeQL, secret scanning, and dependency review; the delegator cannot approve the PR.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Limited / not a first-class snapshot model. Environment state is not persisted or restored between sessions (ephemeral, destroyed each run). Instead, the environment is reproducibly RE-built each session via the .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml workflow (preinstall tools/dependencies, drawing on the GitHub Actions ecosystem of community actions), whose output appears in the session logs. So 'restore' is achieved by deterministic re-provisioning from version-controlled setup steps rather than by saving/restoring a filesystem snapshot. [uncertain] Whether any Actions-style caching of dependencies persists across sessions to speed setup.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Primarily cloud-only for the coding agent (it always runs in GitHub's hosted ephemeral Actions environment; no self-hosting of the agent runtime is described, and it is Linux-runner-only). Handoff to local is via standard Git: pull/checkout the copilot/ branch and continue locally; sessions can be started and tracked from VS Code/JetBrains/Eclipse and the GitHub CLI, and the separate Copilot CLI supports local and remote sessions with cross-device sync. There is no live cloud<->local migration of a single agent session preserving in-memory state.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: The cloud coding agent is single-task per session (one repo, one PR per task; no fan-out of subagents and no multi-PR from one issue). Parallelism is achieved by launching multiple independent agent sessions (e.g., one per issue/task), each in its own isolated ephemeral environment with no shared live state — isolation is by separate environments + separate copilot/ branches, with conflicts resolved through normal Git/PR merge. The Copilot App/CLI/SDK layer adds a UI for managing parallel sessions, quick chats, and issue/PR management. [uncertain] Any hard cap on concurrent sessions (likely bounded by premium-request quota and Actions concurrency limits).
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Highly multi-surface, all converging on issue->PR. Primary trigger: assign a GitHub Issue to Copilot. Also: prompt from VS Code (and JetBrains/Eclipse), the agents panel/page on GitHub.com, the GitHub CLI, Raycast, follow-up prompts and PR comments during a session, and external task tools that integrate assignment — Azure Boards, Jira, Linear, Slack, and Teams can all assign tasks to Copilot. Each task consumes premium requests (one per model request as of June 2025).

implementation.implementation_stack: Identity/auth: GitHub accounts + a scoped GitHub App/bot identity for the agent; org/enterprise policy gating. Execution: GitHub Actions-hosted ephemeral Linux (Ubuntu x64) containers, provisioned via .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml and the Actions community-action catalog; default egress firewall; optional MCP servers for tool access. Persistence: GitHub-native — Git objects (copilot/ branches, signed/verified commits with Agent-Logs-Url trailers), PR/issue data, and session-log storage surfaced across web/IDE/CLI/Raycast. Config: Markdown instruction files (AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md, CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md) and custom agents in .github/agents/*.agent.md. Security tooling: CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency review. Copilot CLI persists sessions in the user's home dir with cross-device sync. [uncertain] Internal databases/storage engines GitHub uses for session logs and agent orchestration are not public.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Copilot Coding Agent is the 'platform-native, repo-scoped, async, ephemeral' archetype and offers several patterns for Labmate. (1) Identity reuse: it binds session identity to an existing account system (GitHub) and runs the agent under a scoped service identity distinct from the user — Labmate can mirror this by binding sessions to the Discord connector identity while executing tools under a scoped service principal, and recording the human as the originator. (2) Ephemeral-execution + durable-artifact split: nothing in the sandbox survives, but durable outputs (branch/PR/logs) live in the system of record. For Labmate this maps to ephemeral active session state in Redis Streams (TTL, discarded at session end) plus durable session documents + final artifacts in MongoDB, with each artifact carrying a back-link to its session log (analogous to the Agent-Logs-Url trailer) for auditability. (3) Reproducible-env-over-snapshot: re-provisioning from a version-controlled setup file (copilot-setup-steps.yml) instead of snapshotting is simpler and is a good model if Labmate's tool environments are deterministic. (4) Instruction layering: the AGENTS.md + copilot-instructions.md + path-specific + org-level cascade with explicit precedence (personal > repo, nearest AGENTS.md wins) is a clean precedence model Labmate can adopt for workspace_id-scoped vs global instructions. (5) Trigger surface: issue/connector assignment as the session-creation API (Discord message/thread == 'assign to agent') matches Labmate's Discord-as-entry-point design; consume-on-trigger quota accounting is also worth emulating. (6) Safety defaults: network-firewall-on-by-default and 'delegator cannot approve' are strong defaults to copy for any autonomous tool-execution path.
